MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Patient ID: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Peripheral blood
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Cystic fibrosis mutation testing
Clinical Notes: Previous request for Alagille syndrome testing noted
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referring Hospital: [redacted location]

TEST PERFORMED
Multiplex oligonucleotide ligation assay (MOLA) screening for 31 CFTR gene mutations

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. Multiplex oligonucleotide ligation assay was performed to screen for 31 common CFTR mutations, covering approximately 95% of cystic fibrosis mutations in Northwest European populations.

MUTATIONS TESTED
The following 31 CFTR mutations were analyzed:
1. F508del (c.1521_1523delCTT)
2. G542X (c.1624G>T)
3. G551D (c.1652G>A)
4. W1282X (c.3846G>A)
5. N1303K (c.3909C>G)
6. R553X (c.1657C>T)
7. 621+1G>T
8. R117H (c.350G>A)
9. 1717-1G>A
10. R347P (c.1040G>C)
11. R334W (c.1000C>T)
12. 3849+10kbC>T
13. 2789+5G>A
14. 3120+1G>A
15. I507del (c.1519_1521delATC)
16. 1898+1G>A
17. 3659delC
18. R560T (c.1679G>C)
19. G85E (c.254G>A)
20. R1162X (c.3484C>T)
21. 2184delA
22. 711+1G>T
23. S549N (c.1646G>A)
24. S549R (c.1645A>C)
25. R347H (c.1040G>A)
26. A455E (c.1364C>A)
27. 2183AA>G
28. Q493X (c.1477C>T)
29. V520F (c.1558G>T)
30. 1078delT
31. 3876delA

RESULTS

CFTR GENE ANALYSIS
Result: No mutations detected

None of the 31 CFTR mutations tested were identified in this patient.

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS
1. DNA has been extracted and stored for potential future testing
2. Previous request for Alagille syndrome testing (JAGGED1 gene) was noted in the referral
3. Alagille syndrome testing is not routinely performed in this laboratory

INTERPRETATION
1. The absence of detectable mutations among the 31 CFTR variants tested does not exclude a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis
2. This panel detects approximately 95% of CF-causing mutations in Northwest European populations
3. The clinical diagnosis of CF has not been confirmed by this testing
4. The likelihood of CF is reduced but not eliminated
5. Approximately 5% of CF patients of Northwest European ancestry may have mutations not covered by this panel

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. If clinical suspicion of cystic fibrosis persists, consider referral to a specialist CF laboratory for:
   - Extended CFTR gene sequencing
   - Deletion/duplication analysis
   - Analysis of rare or population-specific variants

2. For the previously noted Alagille syndrome query:
   - Genetics referral is recommended if clinical diagnosis of Alagille syndrome is confirmed
   - JAGGED1 gene testing can be arranged through specialist laboratories

3. Genetic counseling may be beneficial to discuss:
   - Test limitations
   - Residual risk assessment
   - Testing options for family members if indicated

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
